title: A failed or unreadable screening run looks like a clean one
root_cause: Screening has no single outcome value. _run_analysis keeps only last_error and a parse_status string inside a debug dict (app.py:593-616) and stores GREEN from the alert count alone (app.py:751). main() then rebuilds 'failed', 'complete' and 'not executed' from three separate keys (app.py:1461-1486). So an unreadable reply and a server failure end as GREEN or 'not executed', and Finalize opens with nothing to review (app.py:2230).
owner_decision: When screening failed or its reply could not be read, what should the banner say, and may the visit still be finalized?

title: Lab results have no proper shape: unit, date and source
root_cause: A lab result has no typed shape. The unit lives in the key name (value_umol_per_l, value_copies_per_ml). Anything the add-case parser cannot match exactly, such as another date format, another spelling or a sentence, becomes one untyped narrative blob stamped with the visit date (app.py:940-985). Readers then drop the unit (stage1_summary.py:13-23) or ignore the blob, as the creatinine rule does (alert_rules.py:63).
owner_decision: Should the add-case form make the clinician pick a unit for each lab value, or should the app assume one unit per test (and which for creatinine, mg/dL or umol/L)?
test_idea: Add a TDF case whose labs box says 'Creatinine: 88 umol/L on 2025-12-01' and check that no 'no recent creatinine result found' alert is raised (today it is).

title: Model gets undated notes and 'None recorded' for real labs
root_cause: build_patient_context turns the record into two undated strings: notes_text, with today's note appended unlabelled, and labs_narrative, built from free-text lab entries only (patient_parser.py:73-117). The screening prompt prints them as the whole history and the whole lab list (llm_screening.py:354-363). So patients whose labs are structured are told 'Laboratory results: None recorded', and the model cannot date any note. Patient Details repeats the narrative-only mistake (app.py:1255-1262). test_idea: Build the screening prompt for P002 with a stub client and check that it lists the viral load dated 2025-09-15 and does not say 'Laboratory results: None recorded' (today it says None recorded).

title: Lab age judged against a stale date, or not at all
root_cause: The analysis has no visit date of its own. _run_analysis replaces the note but keeps the date stored when the case was created (app.py:435-437), and no code turns a lab date into an age (stage1_summary.py:31, llm_screening.py:354). So the rules measure recency against an old date, and the model does the date maths itself and gets it wrong (P001's 113-day-old viral load is called over 6 months old in 3 of 3 runs).

test_idea: Build the screening prompt for P001 and check that it states the viral load's age in days against the visit date (today it gives only the raw date).

The rules then test exact list membership ('TDF' in the list, alert_rules.py:60) on those raw pieces, and the agentic subtasks use them too (agentic_flow.py:130). root_cause: The text rules search one joined notes string by plain substring, with no negation or date (alert_rules.py:106-183). title: Saved patient and rule files load as empty and get overwritten

title: In-memory guideline store keeps only the last file
root_cause: InMemoryVectorStore.index_guidelines replaces the whole store on every call (vector_store.py:163-170), while RagEngine.ensure_indexed calls it once per file. create_vector_store swallows any Chroma error and returns that store silently (vector_store.py:252). So if Chroma fails, only the WHO file is searchable for every Ugandan patient, while indexing reports all chunks done. Dangerous for Phase 1 output whenever Chroma fails; the overwrite is a one-line fix worth pulling forward.

title: Guideline searches ignore the patient's actual problems
root_cause: Retrieval queries are built mostly from fixed text. The screening step searches once with the seed 'visit audit checklist labs monitoring regimen' (app.py:517-522). _build_query puts alert fields and a pasted Python dict ahead of the notes, so the embedder cuts the patient text at 254 tokens (rag_engine.py:133-136). Keywords come from plain substrings (rag_engine.py:189), and the agentic subtasks are stock text with the notes first (agentic_flow.py:153, 246). This makes Phase 1 output worse today: P002's false lab alert cites a passage this fixed query returned.
owner_decision: none

root_cause: process_markdown_guidelines stores only page_number and a local source_path on each chunk (guideline_processor.py:299). Nothing records the country, issuing body, title or edition. So retrieval cannot filter by country (rag_engine.py:110), the prompts can't say which guideline governs (llm_screening.py:20, agentic_flow.py:793), every citation reads 'Guidelines, p.N' with same-number pages merged (app.py:1934), and the live plan shows no references at all (app.py:2181). title: Embedder silently falls back to word hashing
root_cause: Embedder.__init__ catches any model-load error and switches to word hashing while model_name still reports the requested model (embedder.py:35), and _get_embedder caches the result (app.py:227). So a typo in the model box or an offline machine collapses search quality with nothing on screen.

title: Chunks are cut by characters past the embedder's limit
root_cause: chunk_page_text cuts 1,200-character windows with a 200-character overlap that starts mid-word (guideline_processor.py:45-101), while MiniLM reads only 254 word pieces. So 42% of chunks are searchable on their opening only, and tables, headings and sentences across page breaks are broken.
owner_decision: How should guideline text be split and stored: plain chunks as today, chunks along the guideline's own sections, or one record per recommendation (plan item 2B.7)?

title: Model sees only the first few hundred characters of passages
root_cause: Each place that shows a passage cuts it to a fixed number of leading characters: 480 in the screening bundle (llm_screening.py:24), one passage of 200 per subtask in the plan prompt (agentic_flow.py:782), and 350 or 600 in explanations (explanation_generator.py:389). So the model reads about half of what was retrieved, often not the sentence that matched. This is tied to the 2B chunk size but cheap to pull forward.
owner_decision: none
test_idea: Build the screening bundle from a 1,200-character chunk, and check that the quote the model sees includes the chunk's last sentence (today it is cut at 480 characters).

root_cause: page_number counts '<!-- PAGE BREAK -->' segments from 1 in every extract file (guideline_processor.py:255, 299). So 'p.22' in the Uganda ART file is printed page 255, both Uganda files use pages 1 to 51, and no cited page can be found in the real document.
owner_decision: Should citations show the printed page of the original guideline (needs a page map per file) or a section heading instead?
test_idea: Check that the chunk holding the Uganda ART text printed on page 255 has page_number 255 (today it is 22).

root_cause: The persistent index is named from truncated file stems (app.py:255-259) and only ever added to, never cleared (vector_store.py:85). An empty guideline list marks indexing done (rag_engine.py:94). So an edited file, a fifth file or a missing folder serves stale or no passages without notice.
owner_decision: none

title: Same patient gets different alerts and colours between runs
root_cause: Both clients sample at temperature 0.2 with no seed (llm_client.py:286), and the visit colour rests on the severity word the model picks (app.py:381-391). So P004's same alert is moderate in two runs and high in one, and the visit flips between YELLOW and RED. Only clinician-labelled cases run several times can say how much variation is acceptable.

test_idea: Run P004 three times, and check that the visit colour is the same in all three runs (today it is RED once and YELLOW twice).

title: Prompt scope leaves out non-drug findings like Kintu's BP rise
root_cause: The screening prompt limits the model to HIV medication safety, with a cap of 5 alerts and an instruction to merge related issues (llm_screening.py:301-341), and no fixed rule reads blood pressure numbers (alert_rules.py:183). So a non-drug finding like Kintu's rise from 118/74 to 138/88 has no path to an alert, although both readings are in the prompt, and nobody is told when the cap was hit.
owner_decision: Should ARTEMIS flag problems outside HIV-drug safety, such as a blood pressure rise, and if so with a fixed rule or by widening the AI's brief?
test_idea: Run Kintu-Test 001 three times, and check that at least one alert mentions blood pressure in every run (today none of the 3 runs does).
